issues.legal_issue: A statutory protection governing eviction in a suit applies to an appeal that is a continuation and rehearing of that suit when the protection takes effect while the appeal is pending.
material_facts: A landlord obtained an eviction decree, and the tenant appealed against it.

While the appeal arising from the eviction suit was pending, a new provision came into force barring an eviction decree in a pending suit or proceeding unless the landlord had the specified written permission.
The High Court treated the appeal as not being a proceeding pending against the tenant because the tenant had filed it.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was a continuation and rehearing of the suit, so the new protection applied to it; the High Court was wrong to conclude that no proceeding was pending against the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal is a rehearing and a continuation of the suit, and the appellate court has seisin of the case; accordingly, the word “suit” in clause 13-A of the C.P. and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949 includes an appeal. The Court relied on Lachmeshwar Prasad Shukul v. Keshwar Lal Chaudhuri, Kristnama Chariar v. Mangammal, Garikapati v. Subbiah Chowdhry, Amarjit Kaur v. Pritam Singh, Lakshmi Narayan Guin v. Niranjan Modak, and H. Shiva Rao v. Cecilia Pereira. It distinguished Motiram Ghelabhai v. Jagan Nagar because the particular repeal-and-saving language there displaced the general continuation-of-suit principle.

predicates.eviction_case_on_appeal: A party is pursuing an appeal arising from a suit seeking the party’s eviction.
predicates.appeal_pending_when_protection_takes_eff: The appeal remains pending when a new eviction protection takes effect.
predicates.protection_requires_permission_before_ev: The new protection bars eviction in the relevant pending proceeding unless the landlord obtains written permission.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal is pending as a new permission-based protection takes effect, the tenant receives that protection in the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: Applying a new eviction requirement to a proceeding pending when it takes effect is not necessarily retrospective merely because the proceeding arose from an earlier cause of action.
material_facts: The eviction suit and the decree preceded the amendments that expanded the definition of covered premises and introduced the permission requirement.
The permission requirement took effect while an appeal arising from the suit was pending.
The High Court treated the amendments as inapplicable because they were prospective and the tenancy had ended before they took effect.
issues.conclusion: The amendments could operate on the pending proceeding without being retrospective: the permission requirement governed future enforcement and did not undo anything done in the past. The High Court was wrong to disregard the amendments on that basis, and the matter was remitted for fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: A provision may be prospective in force yet have retroactive operation on a pending proceeding where it imposes a requirement for future enforcement without affecting past acts or existing rights. Statutes providing new remedies for enforcement of an existing right may apply to past as well as future causes of action. The Court relied on Commissioners of Customs and Excise v. Thorn Electrical Industries Ltd. in explaining that a law is not retrospective merely because a condition for its future operation draws on antecedent events. It also held that the amended definition of “premises” in clause 2(4-A) and the requirement in clause 13-A of the C.P. and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949 could not be ignored while an eviction proceeding was pending.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_pending_when_new_req: An eviction suit or proceeding, including an appeal arising from it, remains pending when a new requirement takes effect.
predicates.new_requirement_governs_future_enforceme: The new requirement regulates what must be done to enforce an eviction outcome in the future.
predicates.past_acts_remain_undisturbed: Applying the new requirement does not undo or alter acts completed before it took effect.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding is pending, a new requirement governs future enforcement, and past acts remain undisturbed, the requirement applies to the pending proceeding without retrospective effect.
